clue.text: Row produced by fellow losing heart in dark

parts.note: a row is a loud noise, a din

indicators.note: the word for fellow drops its central letter

parts.note: a guy is a man, a fellow

explanation.surface: A quarrel breaks out with a man who has lost his nerve, somewhere in the dark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'losing heart' takes the middle U out of GUY, leaving GY.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a dingy room is drab and gloomy, poorly lit.

clue.text: Extract — it is filling cap when overturned

indicators.note: the whole assembly is turned upside down, which in a down clue reads it bottom to top
the contraction goes into the middle of the cap word

parts.note: a lid is a cap or cover
contracted, it is becomes it's, written without the apostrophe

explanation.surface: An instruction for getting something out: fill a cap and tip it over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when overturned' reverses the whole assembly, so the cap reads backwards as well as the contraction inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to distil something is to extract its essence.

clue.text: Born without any commotion, receiving food initially as a necessity

parts.note: née, born, marks a woman's maiden name

indicators.note: the dull adverb takes in a letter

parts.note: doing something dully means with no excitement or fuss

indicators.note: only the opening letter of food is used

explanation.surface: A birth with no fuss, and the baby fed first because it must be.
explanation.walkthrough: F (first of food) goes into DULLY after its D: DFULLY.
explanation.definitionFit: Adverb match: done needfully means done because it is required, of necessity.

clue.text: Long run's central section cut after expression of acquiescence

indicators.note: the shortened run comes after the yes

parts.note: yea is an old word for yes

indicators.note: the middle letter of the word for run is taken out

parts.note: the word run, its 's a link

explanation.surface: A long run gets shortened in the middle after someone says yes.
explanation.walkthrough: RUN minus its middle U gives RN.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to long for something is to yearn, to crave it.

clue.text: Trouble — being taken to Judge — may lead to this?

definitions.text: Trouble — being taken to Judge — may lead to this?

indicators.note: the trouble word is attached to the judge letter

parts.note: to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Getting into trouble and being hauled before a judge could end in prison.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition: trouble that reaches a judge may end in prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a prison sentence is where a court case over trouble may end.

clue.text: Jazz pianist's explosive pitch and endlessly increased sound quality (endlessly)

parts.note: jelly is slang for gelignite
a ship pitches and rolls

indicators.note: the word for increased loses its final letter

parts.note: more means increased, extra

indicators.note: the second instance again drops the last letter of the sound word

parts.note: tone is the quality of a sound

explanation.surface: A review of a jazz pianist: explosive, with a sound that keeps getting bigger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jazz pianist's' is 'jazz pianist is'. MOR(E) and TON(E) lose their last letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Proper name: Jelly Roll Morton was an early New Orleans jazz pianist and composer.

clue.text: Unrest militants organised? One plays along

indicators.note: being organised means put into a new order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is the unrest among militants actually organised by someone?
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an instrumentalist plays an instrument, often accompanying a singer.

clue.text: Shell helping to teach us knowledge

indicators.note: a helping is a portion, so the answer is a portion of the following words

explanation.surface: Helping to teach us knowledge sounds like a school's mission statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a husk is the dry outer covering of a seed.

clue.text: Inappropriate nude frolics around university

indicators.note: the shuffled letters go around the letter for university
frolicking is romping about, so the letters of nude move

explanation.surface: Naked high jinks on campus are thought unsuitable.
explanation.walkthrough: NUDE becomes UNDE and U goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: something undue is unwarranted or improper, more than is fitting.

clue.text: Fortress post, timeless memorial

parts.note: a keep is the main tower of a castle

indicators.note: T, for time, is taken out

parts.note: a stake is a wooden post

explanation.surface: A castle's post serving as a lasting monument.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a keepsake is a small memento kept to remember someone.

clue.text: Page in pad pen defaced about to be taken up

indicators.note: spoiled letters are rearranged
in a down clue taken up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A page in a notepad has been scribbled over by a pen.
explanation.walkthrough: PADPEN rearranges to ENDPAP; RE reversed gives ER.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific type: an endpaper is the blank leaf pasted inside a book's cover.

clue.text: Enthusiastic comment about coastal resort denies esplanade is ruined

indicators.note: a ruined thing is broken up, so its letters are reassembled

explanation.surface: Someone rejects praise for a seaside town, pointing out that its promenade is a wreck.
explanation.definitionFit: Idiom: the saying holds that the Italian city is so beautiful you can die content after visiting it.

clue.text: Childhood dreaming?

definitions.meaning: read as two words, being ... is being in imagination, daydreaming

explanation.surface: Childhood as a time of daydreams.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym plus split reading: early infancy, and 'in fancy' meaning lost in imagination.

clue.text: Put down most of rusty iron

indicators.note: the colour word loses its last letter

parts.note: rust is reddish, so rusty suggests red
to press clothes is to iron them

explanation.surface: Putting away an old, mostly rusted iron.
explanation.definitionFit: Verb synonym: to put down a rebellion is to repress or crush it.

clue.text: Senior politician coming round not quite after time for speaking venue

indicators.note: the politician's letters go round the rest

parts.note: PM, Prime Minister

indicators.note: the last letter of the lateness word is cut

parts.note: late means after the expected time
taken as written

explanation.surface: A senior politician comes back round, a bit late, for a speaking engagement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' trims only the word for 'after time'; 'for' is taken as written.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a platform is a raised stage from which speakers address an audience.

clue.text: Sign from landlord — hurried in, inclined to indulge

indicators.note: the hurrying word goes inside the sign

parts.note: a To Let sign advertises a property for rent
ran means hurried

explanation.surface: Someone dashes in seeing the landlord's sign, keen to treat themselves.
explanation.walkthrough: TO LET is the British sign on a property available for rent.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a tolerant person is lenient, willing to put up with or allow things.

clue.text: Fool covering recipe in cream

indicators.note: the letter goes inside the word for cream

parts.note: the cream, or pick, is the best of something
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A fool, the creamy pudding, covering a recipe written up in cream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fool' looks like the dessert, as does 'cream'; it is a slang insult. 'covering' just joins definition to wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: a prick is a vulgar term for a stupid or contemptible person.

clue.text: Government funds? I note a sign of affection about old plane

indicators.note: the kiss and A sit next to the old plane

parts.note: the Comet was the first jet airliner, from the 1950s
X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: Someone sends a kiss about an old aircraft, wondering who pays for government.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: tax on earnings is a main source of the state's revenue.

clue.text: Flowering plant caught invading ragged bush is one?

indicators.note: the cricket letter for caught enters among the words bush is before the jumbling
ragged means untidy, so the letters are messed up

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
the Roman numeral I is one

explanation.surface: Is the flowering plant caught up in a scruffy bush one of them?
explanation.walkthrough: 'invading' adds C to BUSHIS, with I for 'one'; 'ragged' rearranges all eight letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Genus: hibiscus is a shrub with large showy trumpet-shaped flowers.

clue.text: Distinctly gutted overwhelmed by awful poem

indicators.note: the remaining letters are engulfed by the word for awful

parts.note: ill means bad, awful

indicators.note: with its insides removed, only the first and last letters remain

explanation.surface: Someone clearly devastated, overcome by a terrible poem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gutted' reads as 'devastated' but means the word loses its insides.
explanation.definitionFit: Genre: an idyll is a short poem describing a peaceful rural scene.

clue.text: Recalled list of runners occupying street? Trotters more relevant here

indicators.note: the reversed word sits inside the street

parts.note: a lane is a narrow street

indicators.note: called back, so the card word is read backwards

parts.note: a race card lists the horses in each race

explanation.surface: A list of racehorses on a street, where trotting horses would be more at home.
explanation.walkthrough: CARD reversed gives DRAC. 'Trotters' are not trotting horses but pigs' feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: the Landrace is a pig breed, and pigs' feet are called trotters.

clue.text: Pursuit heading off with regret? Not to be believed

indicators.note: the first letter is removed

parts.note: a hunt is a pursuit
to rue is to regret

explanation.surface: A chase called off amid regrets, and the story behind it is dubious.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: an untrue claim is false and should not be credited.

clue.text: Note iron amongst molten ditto — hot place

indicators.note: the note and symbol go among the other letters
melted metal flows into a new shape, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: ditto repeats the previous word, iron
Fe is the chemical symbol for iron

explanation.surface: A note about iron inside a molten mass of the same metal: very hot indeed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditto' stands for 'iron'; 'molten' rearranges IRON to IRNO, and NFE goes in after the I.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: an inferno is a blazing fire, or hell itself.

clue.text: Fine and fit? I wouldn't believe it

parts.note: F stands for fine, as on pencil grades
able means fit, capable

explanation.surface: A sceptic hears someone is fine and fit and refuses to believe it.
explanation.definitionFit: Description: a fable is a made-up tale, something incredible or untrue.

clue.text: A black mound, new, will do for stomach

parts.note: B is black, as on pencils
a dome is a rounded mound

explanation.surface: A dark rounded bulge, freshly appeared, will pass for a belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: the abdomen is the belly region, containing the stomach.

clue.text: Religious belief is restricted by endless protest

indicators.note: the word is is held within the shortened protest
the protest word loses its last letter

parts.note: a demo is a protest march

explanation.surface: A faith hemmed in by continuous protest.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' looks like 'unceasing' but means the protest word loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Specific belief: deism holds that a creator exists but does not intervene in the world.

clue.text: Politician strangely reminiscent? A bit

indicators.note: something strange is out of order, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone finds a politician oddly familiar, just slightly.
explanation.definitionFit: Example: a member of the cabinet is a senior government politician.

clue.text: Action taken is severe, halving supply of energy

indicators.note: the pair of E letters, E standing for energy, is cut to one

parts.note: steep means severe, as in a steep fine

explanation.surface: A harsh measure that cuts the energy supply in half.
explanation.walkthrough: STEEP has two Es; halving them leaves one.
explanation.definitionFit: Synonym: a step is a measure or action taken towards something.

clue.text: Kilo in no way a measure of speed

parts.note: K is kilo in the NATO alphabet
not means in no way

explanation.surface: A kilo is not a measure of speed at all.
explanation.definitionFit: Unit: a knot is one nautical mile per hour, used for ships and aircraft.

clue.text: Courage that is shown by male farm animal

parts.note: an ox is a farm animal
i.e. abbreviates id est, that is

explanation.surface: Bravery, that is, as displayed by a bull.
explanation.definitionFit: Slang synonym: moxie is American slang for nerve and determination.
